subject: Role Sculpting Proposal — Compute Reliability Team
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Nadia Rivera <nadia@talentbridge.co>
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Role Sculpting Proposal — Compute Reliability Team

Team —

I'm sharing an initial proposal for role scope changes and a sensitive headcount reallocation across the Compute Reliability squad. This is prompted by a persistent coverage gap on long-running infra projects and an upcoming round of performance reviews (mid-November) where we need clarity on role expectations.

High level summary (see attached PDF and Drive link for full diff):
- Reduce the "Senior Platform Engineer" role count by 1 and create:
  - 1 Reliability Lead (IC4+) focused on cross-cluster SLO ownership, incident strategy, and vendor escalation.
  - 1 Platform Specialist (IC3-IC4) focused on kernel-level optimization and day-to-day runtime performance improvements.
- Re-scope two existing positions: move on-call primary from Team Alpha to Team Beta (6-month pilot).
- Create a short feedback window before comp/leveling decisions — we propose a 10-business-day window after the performance calibration meeting for appeals.

Why this matters now:
- Recent incidents exposed a lack of a single owner for platform latency regressions.
- Upcoming dedicated customer commitments will require a named reliability contact.
- We need to minimize churn during review cycles and avoid ad-hoc lateral moves that create coverage cliffs.

As this involves potentially sensitive reassignments and a reduction in one senior headcount, I want to be deliberate about the comms cadence and the HR/legal guardrails. Specific asks:
1) Olga — can People Ops confirm appropriate notice language, severance baseline, and performance appeal process constraints?
2) Grace — do you want to brief execs with the high-level rationale or shall we route via you after we solidify the timelines?
3) Marcus — please validate coverage assumptions and whether the on-call pilot is feasible without hiring additional temps.
4) Nadia/Workwise — can you review the attached role delta PDF and flag anything risky in terms of compliance or best practice?

Proposed timeline (tentative):
- Oct 25: Internal review + HR redlines
- Nov 2: Finalize role descriptions and compensation bands
- Nov 9–13: Performance calibration & appeals window opens
- Nov 16: Announce assignments and updated org chart (staged rollout)

Attachments: 2026-10-25-compute-role-deltas.pdf (diff), drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cComputeRoleDeltas

Note: keep this thread limited to the recipients above for now — we'll expand only when the comms draft is approved.

Thanks,
Jonas

Jonas Weber
Staff Engineer, Compute Reliability

Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Role Sculpting Proposal — Compute Reliability Team

Thanks for the clear outline, Jonas. I reviewed the PDF and flagged three HR/legal concerns inline:

- Severance baseline: our standard for a role-level reduction at IC4 is 8–12 weeks; if the impacted headcount has >5y tenure we should consider 12 weeks.
- Performance appeal window: 10 business days is tight. Recommend 15 business days to ensure RR/appeal owners have time to review calibration evidence.
- Communication sequencing: we must separate individual reassignment conversations from any role-elimination notices. Draft comm templates attached (comm-template-deltas.docx).

Operational recommendations:
- Use a two-week "quiet sync" with the affected manager before any public announcement. That gives managers time to prepare 1:1 talking points and to surface any candidate for lateral moves.
- For the on-call pilot, require a written contingency plan (backup rotation + hiring trigger) before shifting primary responsibility.

On legal/compliance: Workwise suggests a quick audit of any prior PII accesses for the individuals potentially impacted (standard process) — I copied Workwise so they can advise on that step.

I'll incorporate these redlines into a single doc and push back a new timeline — expect it by Tue, Oct 28 EOD.

—Olga

Olga Petrov
Director, Talent Strategy (interim)

Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Role Sculpting Proposal — Compute Reliability Team

Appreciate the clear proposal. A few technical notes from my side after running coverage sims against current tickets:
- If we move primary on-call from Alpha -> Beta, Alpha will lose 18% of deep-dive incident capacity. That is acceptable for 6 months only if we hold two open hiring reqs (one contract engineer; one IC3) as a contingency.
- The Reliability Lead should have explicit responsibility for the dedicated-customer SLA pathing; add that to the role bullets.
- Suggest we convert the proposed Platform Specialist into a hybrid role for the pilot (3 months) so we can re-evaluate scope post-pilot. This minimizes headcount disruption if it doesn't land.

Action items I can take:
- Draft the updated role bullets and a one-page coverage contingency (will send by Wed 10/28).
- Update the hiring triggers for the Finance and Capacity teams so we have a fast-track if coverage dips below threshold.

Finally, we should ensure engineers who will be candidates for lateral moves have at least 3 options considered before any severance decisions. Helps with retention and reduces legal risk.

-Marcus

Thanks all for the rapid turn. After reading the proposed changes and the HR redlines:

I approve moving forward with a staged approach in line with Olga's recommendations. Conditions:
- Extend the appeal window to 15 business days.
- Final role bullets must include the Reliability Lead SLA ownership (Marcus to add).
- A contingency hiring trigger must be documented and pre-approved by Capacity finance before any on-call move.

Jonas — please coordinate final comms with Olga and Nadia. Use the comm-template-deltas.docx as the public-facing version and work with legal on any language that references severance or performance.

Once Olga posts the consolidated timeline (expected 10/28 EOD), let's schedule a 30-minute exec sync (I can host) the week of Nov 8 to sign off on the public announcement.

I'll keep this limited to the current list until we have the comm draft. Thanks for keeping this tight and operational.

Grace O'Connor
VP, Product & Platform
